import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 848

Is the maximum size of a set $A \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$ such that $ab + 1$ is never
squarefree (for all $a, b \in A$) achieved by taking those $n \equiv 7 \pmod{25}$?

*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/848](https://www.erdosproblems.com/848)
 - [Er92b] Erdős, P. "Some of my favourite problems in number theory, combinatorics,
   and geometry." Resenhas do Instituto de Matemático e Estatística da Universidade
   de São Paulo 2.2 (1995): 165-186.
 - [Sa25] Sawhney, M. "Problem 848." (2025)
   https://www.math.columbia.edu/~msawhney/Problem_848.pdf
 - Full formal proof of asymptotic result: https://github.com/The-Obstacle-Is-The-Way/erdos-banger
-/

namespace Erdos848

/-- A set $A$ has the non-squarefree product property if $ab + 1$ is not squarefree
for all $a, b ∈ A$. -/
def NonSquarefreeProductProp (A : Finset ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ a ∈ A, ∀ b ∈ A, ¬Squarefree (a * b + 1)

/-- The candidate extremal set: $\{n ∈ \{0, \dots, N-1\} : n ≡ 7 (mod 25)\}$. -/
def A₇ (N : ℕ) : Finset ℕ :=
  (Finset.range N).filter (fun n => n % 25 = 7)

/-- The Erdős Problem 848 statement for a fixed $N$: any set $A ⊆ \{0, \dots, N-1\}$ with
the non-squarefree product property has cardinality at most $|A₇(N)|$. -/
def Erdos848For (N : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ A : Finset ℕ, A ⊆ Finset.range N → NonSquarefreeProductProp A →
    A.card ≤ (A₇ N).card

/-- Is the maximum size of a set $A ⊆ \{1, \dots, N\}$ such that $ab + 1$ is never squarefree
(for all $a, b ∈ A$) achieved by taking those $n ≡ 7 \pmod{25}$?

This asks whether `Erdos848 N` holds for all $N$ (formulated using `A ⊆ Finset.range N`).

This was solved for all sufficiently large $N$ by Sawhney in this note. In fact, Sawhney proves
something slightly stronger, that there exists some constant $c>0$ such that if
$\lvert A\rvert \geq (\frac{1}{25}-c)N$ and $N$ is large then $A$ is contained in either
$\{ n\equiv 7\pmod{25}\}$ or $\{n\equiv 18\pmod{25}\}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_848 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ N, Erdos848For N := by
  sorry

/-- There exists $N₀$ such that for all $N ≥ N₀$, if $A ⊆ \{1, \dots, N\}$ satisfies that $ab + 1$
is never squarefree for all $a, b ∈ A$, then $|A| ≤ |\{n ≤ N : n ≡ 7 \pmod{25}\}|$.

More precisely, Sawhney proves: there exist absolute constants $η > 0$ and $N₀$
such that for all $N ≥ N₀$, if $|A| ≥ (1/25 - η)N$ then $A ⊆ \{n : n ≡ 7 \pmod{25}\}$ or
$A ⊆ \{n : n ≡ 18 \pmod{25}\}$.

A complete formal Lean 4 proof is available at:
https://github.com/The-Obstacle-Is-The-Way/erdos-banger -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/The-Obstacle-Is-The-Way/erdos-banger/blob/1cc2ac8e9d70516e979733c6ea5c4d2eb652d1f5/formal/lean/Erdos/848.lean"]
theorem erdos_848.variants.asymptotic : ∀ᶠ N in Filter.atTop, Erdos848For N := by
  sorry

end Erdos848

findings.description: The bibliography entry labelled [Er92b] (lines 27–29) identifies the wrong paper. It gives the title and publication details of Erdős's 1995 Resenhas article, which the source bibliography calls [Er95], rather than the 1992 paper cited for Problem 848. This does not affect the Lean mathematics.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/848 cites [Er92b, p.239]. The bibliography at https://www.erdosproblems.com/bibs/Er92b identifies this as “Some of my favourite problems in various branches of combinatorics,” Le Matematiche 47 (1992), 231–240. Problem 23 on page 239 of that paper asks whether the sequence congruent to 7 modulo 25 is maximal when a_i a_j + 1 is never squarefree. The entry at /bibs/Er95 instead matches the file's 1995 citation.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the [Er92b] entry with: Erdős, P., “Some of my favourite problems in various branches of combinatorics,” Le Matematiche 47(2) (1992), 231–240, Problem 23, p.239.

status_issues.recorded: @[category research solved] and answer(True) for the assertion ∀ N, Erdos848For N.
status_issues.source_status: The source currently labels the full question “DECIDABLE — Resolved up to a finite check.” Sawhney's 2025 result proves the assertion only for sufficiently large N; the remaining finite cases are not recorded as settled.
status_issues.evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/848 gives the DECIDABLE status and says “This was solved for all sufficiently large N by Sawhney.” Proposition 1.1 of https://www.math.columbia.edu/~msawhney/Problem_848.pdf explicitly introduces a threshold N₀. The pinned external Lean file likewise says it proves the asymptotic result, not the full all-N conjecture.
status_issues.suggested_change: Change the main theorem to category research open and answer(sorry) unless a completed finite verification can be cited. Keep the universal question itself unchanged. The asymptotic variant's research solved tag and statement are appropriate.

reformulations.difference: The definition states only a universal cardinality upper bound, whereas the source asks whether the candidate set achieves the maximum.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The candidate A₇ N is contained in Finset.range N and is admissible: if a ≡ b ≡ 7 modulo 25, then ab + 1 ≡ 50 ≡ 0 modulo 25, so it is not squarefree. Consequently, bounding every admissible set by the candidate's cardinality is equivalent to saying that the candidate attains the maximum. This was proved as Review848.bound_iff_attains_max in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: The Lean uses {0,…,N−1} and quantifies over all natural N, rather than using the source's interval {1,…,N}.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: An admissible set cannot contain 0, since the diagonal pair (0,0) would require 1 not to be squarefree. Thus the source's fixed-bound assertion for N is equivalent to Erdos848For (N+1), with exactly the same candidate set. Erdos848For 0 is true because the ambient set is empty. Reindexing therefore gives an equivalence of the two all-N assertions. Review848.all_index_equiv proves this without using either sorry-backed theorem.

reformulations.difference: The Lean uses eventual truth along Filter.atTop on ℕ, with the shifted interval convention, rather than an explicit threshold N₀ as in Sawhney's Proposition 1.1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Filter.eventually_atTop on ℕ is equivalent to ∃ N₀, ∀ N ≥ N₀, P N. Applying the fixed-bound equivalence between the source assertion at N and Erdos848For (N+1), and shifting the threshold, gives exactly Proposition 1.1. Review848.eventual_index_equiv proves the equivalence. The linked formal proof also has definitions identical to the file's and concludes ∃ N₀, ∀ N ≥ N₀, Problem848Statement N.
